claims.claim: Polycarp was a Christian bishop of Smyrna in the 2nd century.
Polycarp was born in 69 AD and died in 155 AD.
Polycarp was a disciple of John the Apostle.
The Epistle of Polycarp to the Philippians is addressed to the early Christian church in Philippi.
The epistle is widely believed to be a composite of material written at two different times, in the first half of the second century.
The epistle acted as a covering letter for a collection of writings by Ignatius of Antioch, whose works were being collected by the church at Philippi after Ignatius' visit there.
Scholars generally agree that the epistle is an authentic epistle of Polycarp.
The epistle is the only extant document among a number believed to have been written by Polycarp.

Irenaeus described the epistle as 'a forceful epistle written by Polycarp to the Philippians, from which those who wish to do so, and are anxious about their salvation, can learn the character of his faith, and the preaching of the truth.'
Polycarp did not characterize himself as the bishop of Smyrna anywhere in his letter, but that is what he was.
As bishop, Polycarp seems to be primus inter pares among the presbyters.
